Subject: Potential white‑label partnership — Acme x Redwood

Hi Mina,

Hope you’re well — I’m Alex, Head of Partnerships at Acme Analytics. We’ve been evaluating several inference platforms for a white‑label embedding that we want to surface inside Acme Insights (our SaaS analytics product). Redwood’s performance and private deployment options looked promising from your public docs.

High level: we want to embed model outputs (assistive insights, summarization, Q/A) under our brand (no Redwood logo / custom domain), with controls for data residency and audit logs. Key asks up front:
- Is a white‑label OEM package possible (covering hosted + private deployment for pilots)?
- What are the typical commercial guardrails for revenue share vs fixed fee pilots?
- Any preliminary SOC2 / security artifacts you can share?

Can we book a 30‑min intro next week? I’ll loop in our product lead and procurement if you’re open. I’ve attached a short product one‑pager for context.

Thanks,
Alex Rivera
Head of Partnerships, Acme Analytics

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>

Alex / Mina — quick technical checklist ahead of discovery so we can make the call productive. A few clarifying questions:

1) Traffic and performance
   • Expected concurrent requests and peak TPS?
   • Average prompt length (tokens) and average generated tokens per response?

2) Integration pattern
   • Embedded inference via server‑side calls from Acme backend, or client‑side proxied requests?
   • Do you need streaming responses for UI (token‑by‑token) or full response per call?

3) Deployment & security
   • Would you prefer Redwood Hosted with white‑labeling (custom domain + CSS removal) or Redwood Private (VPC/on‑prem) for pilot?
   • KMS/HSM: are you required to bring your own keys?
   • Audit/log retention requirements (eg 90/365 days)?

4) Compliance
   • SOC2 is expected; do you need a SOC2 report copy or specific control attestation?

5) Data handling
   • Will you send PII or proprietary code as prompts? Need to know classification for caching/retention policy.

If you can reply with the bullets above before our call it will speed up a feasibility read. I’ll prepare a short runbook showing latency estimates for typical model families and our recommended pilot configuration (dedicated small pool vs hosted with B2B QoS).

Thanks — Jonas
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Rivera <alex@acme-analytics.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Sep 2025 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Potential white‑label partnership — Acme x Redwood

Thanks Jonas — answers below, plus a few asks from procurement.

Traffic and performance:
- Target pilot: ~1.2M tokens / month, spiking up to 200 concurrent requests during business hours. Avg prompt ~120 tokens; avg generation ~80 tokens.

Integration pattern:
- Server‑side calls from Acme backend. Streaming is nice but not required for pilot.

Deployment & security:
- For the pilot we prefer Redwood Hosted with white‑labeling (custom domain + brand removal). If pilot succeeds, we will evaluate Redwood Private for full roll‑out.
- We prefer customer‑managed keys (KMS) for production; pilot can use Redwood KMS.
- Audit/log retention: 180 days minimum.

Compliance:
- Please share SOC2 report and your data processing addendum.

Data handling:
- Prompts will include proprietary business metrics (no raw PII). We need confirmation on caching behavior and ability to disable model caching for specific routes.

Procurement notes:
- Procurement looped in — they’ll want a draft SOW and estimated commercial range so they can line‑up internal approvals.

I’ve attached our security requirements doc for reference. Looking forward to the discovery call — propose Tues 9/9 at 10am PT?

Best,
Alex Rivera
Head of Partnerships, Acme Analytics
[Attachment: acme-security-reqs.pdf (pdf)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Alex / Procurement team — great to be working with you. Per our call earlier today (thanks everyone), here’s a concise next steps summary and a preliminary commercial outline so procurement has something to review quickly. I’ve attached a draft SOW for pilot scope.

Summary / commitments:
- Pilot scope (30 days): white‑label hosted pilot for Acme Insights, up to 1.5M tokens during pilot window, 180‑day audit log retention, option to migrate to Private for full roll‑out.
- Security: we’ll provide SOC2 Type II report and DPA. Pilot will use Redwood KMS; production supports customer‑managed KMS. Caching can be disabled per route.
- Branding: white‑labeling to remove Redwood references; custom domain support included in pilot.

Commercial (pilot only):
- Pilot setup fee: $8,000 (one time) — covers configuration, onboarding, and basic white‑labeling work.
- Pilot usage: $0.015 / 1k tokens for pilot usage over baseline (first 1.5M included).
- Post‑pilot: commercial options include committed reserved capacity (monthly) or usage pricing; we’ll provide a tailored proposal if pilot metrics justify Private deployment.

Next steps for procurement:
1) Review attached SOW (SOW-Acme-Redwood-draft.docx) and provide contract contact for redlines.
2) If acceptable, sign pilot SOW (we can send via DocuSign) and schedule onboarding workshop.
3) Jonas will share a short runbook and recommended rate limits for initial traffic.

Doc links: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link-acme-redwood-collab
DocuSign: https://docusign.com/placeholder/ACME-SOW-001

If procurement has budget cycle constraints, flag them and we’ll try to accommodate timing.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
